- TAP v0 files are correctly parsed: each byte represents a pulse half-period in units of 8 system clock cycles.
- A byte value of 0 in TAP v0 indicates the next 3 bytes form a 24-bit little-endian overflow value.
- TAP v1 files use an extended header and the same pulse encoding with improved overflow handling.
- The TAP header (magic bytes, version, platform, video standard, data length) is validated on load.
- Tape images can be mounted and unmounted at runtime via `ITapeUnit.Mount()`/`ITapeUnit.Eject()`.
- Writing to TAP format captures the pulse timing from emulated writes.
- The platform byte in the header distinguishes C64, VIC-20, and C16/Plus4 tapes.

- No cassette port: tape-related I/O port bits behave differently (cassette sense always reads "no tape").
- Built-in 1541 drive: device 8 is always present.
- The 6510 I/O port bit 4 (cassette sense) is permanently pulled high.

The TAP file format stores raw tape pulse timing data. TAP v0 stores pulse lengths as single bytes (with 0 indicating an overflow requiring 3 additional bytes). TAP v1 extends the overflow encoding. The emulator shall read and write both TAP format versions.

- Writing to TAP format captures the pulse timing from emulated writes.
- The platform byte in the header distinguishes C64, VIC-20, and C16/Plus4 tapes.

- Tape reading at normal speed produces identical results to real hardware.
- The timing accuracy supports both PAL and NTSC system clock rates.

expected.description:
The MOS 6510 processor's built-in I/O port at addresses $0000 (data direction register) and $0001 (data port) shall be emulated. This port controls the PLA memory banking configuration (LORAM, HIRAM, CHAREN bits), the cassette motor, and the cassette sense line. The data port shall exhibit the correct behavior with pull-up/pull-down resistors and the capacitive discharge timing that affects reads of output pins.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Address $0000 is the Data Direction Register (DDR); bits set to 1 configure the corresponding $0001 bit as output.
- Address $0001 bits 0-2 (LORAM, HIRAM, CHAREN) control PLA banking and are reflected immediately in the address space configuration.
- Bit 3 controls the cassette motor (active low).
- Bit 4 reads the cassette switch sense (active low).
- Bit 5 is unused on C64 but reads as expected based on DDR/pull-up behavior.
- When a bit transitions from output to input, the capacitive discharge timing (approximately 350 microseconds to decay) is modeled.
- The `IMemoryMappedDevice` interface exposes the port to the address decoder.

expected.description:
Many commercial C64 programs used turbo tape loaders that employ faster pulse encoding than the standard Commodore format. The emulator shall support turbo loaders by providing accurate tape read timing down to individual clock cycles.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Turbo loaders using shorter pulse widths than standard (down to approximately 160 cycles per pulse) function correctly.
- Common turbo formats (Novaload, Biturbo, Turbotape, Cyberload, Pavloda) load successfully.
- Custom pulse encoding schemes are supported through accurate pulse-level emulation.
- The CIA FLAG input timing is accurate to 1 system clock cycle.
- Half-wave and full-wave detection methods both work correctly.
- Multi-speed loaders (that change pulse rates mid-load) are supported.

criteriaLedger.beforeText: Drive STOP, START, FORWARD, REWIND, and RECORD from a known STOP state with no image, read-only image, and writable image. Each accepted mode and tape-sense transition matches pinned VICE. No-image RECORD and read-only-image RECORD leave mode and sense unchanged; accepted RECORD with writable media asserts sense.
criteriaLedger.afterText: From known STOP, cover STOP, START, FORWARD, REWIND and RECORD with absent, read-only and writable images. Match accepted mode and sense. Absent-image and read-only-image RECORD do not change mode or sense; accepted writable RECORD asserts sense when the datasette is enabled.

criteriaLedger.beforeText: For identical accepted tape-sense transitions, C64 CPU port $0001 input bit 4 and VIC-20 VIA1 port A input bit 6 match pinned VICE, including input/output direction masking. C64 CIA1 FLAG and VIC-20 VIA2 CA1 pulse events are tested separately and are not substituted for tape-sense input.
criteriaLedger.afterText: Match C64 CPU port $0001 input bit 4 and VIC-20 VIA1 port A input bit 6, including DDR/output masking. Separately match C64 CIA1 FLAG and VIC-20 VIA2 CA1 pulse routing; sense is not an interrupt pulse.

criteriaLedger.beforeText: With an initially stopped motor and no pending datasette alarm, a motor-on transition schedules the startup read alarm at the current emulated clock plus 32000. The ordered read-side event trace immediately before, at, and after that deadline matches pinned VICE. A pre-existing pending alarm is preserved as VICE preserves it; metadata retrieval alone is not counted as a pulse event.
criteriaLedger.afterText: A stopped motor with no pending alarm schedules the ordinary startup callback at current clock plus 32000; retain an existing alarm as VICE does. FORWARD/REWIND commands schedule their 1000-cycle alarm independently of motor-running state, including motor-on before and after that alarm dispatch. Compare ordered scheduled and actual events, not a pulse-duration getter. Also cover START while the motor is already running, with absent, read-only and writable media, with no pending alarm and with an existing pending alarm. The command reaches the start helper after resetting the gap: install t+32000 only when no alarm is pending, otherwise preserve the existing alarm; match attached-image seek, current-clock write-clock seeding and write-bit zeroing, including clock zero. Contrast START with running-motor FORWARD/REWIND, whose earlier t+1000 alarm survives the helper, and preserve any stop deadline that the command does not clear.

criteriaLedger.beforeText: For a running motor, motor-off schedules stopping at current clock plus 32000 without stopping immediately. Motor-on before that stop executes cancels the pending stop without imposing a new startup ramp. Repeated motor-off does not extend an existing stop deadline. Ordered boundary events and restart after an executed stop match pinned VICE.
criteriaLedger.afterText: Motor-off on a running motor sets a stop deadline of current clock plus 32000 without immediate stopping or replacing an already pending alarm. Actual stopping occurs when a datasette callback observes the deadline reached. Cover callbacks before, at and beyond the deadline, active read rescheduling, STOP with a retained later alarm, repeated off preserving the deadline, and motor-on cancellation even after the deadline but before stop execution. A stopped motor starts again through the native pending-alarm rule. Explicitly include motor-on before the stop deadline and at the deadline before callback dispatch, preserving the already-running motor, pending alarm and write state while clearing the stop deadline; neither case starts a new ramp.

criteriaLedger.beforeText: Recording writes occur only under the native combination of an attached image, accepted RECORD mode, running motor, and qualifying write-line transition. No image, read-only media that rejected RECORD, wrong mode, motor stopped, repeated levels, and nonqualifying transitions produce the same absence of tape writes as pinned VICE.
criteriaLedger.afterText: Recording eligibility follows attached image, accepted RECORD mode, the native running-motor flag and qualifying zero-to-nonzero write-line transition. The running flag is set immediately on motor-on and retained until the delayed-stop callback. Cover writes during startup and pending stop, no writes after executed stop, rejected RECORD, repeated/opposite edges, and retained write-line updates even while ineligible.

criteriaLedger.beforeText: For identical accepted recording signal traces and media, emitted TAP bytes, elapsed-gap/remainder handling, first-write state, image-position updates, and failure/STOP side effects match pinned VICE. Cover short and long gap boundaries and partial or failed writes; an incremented managed pulse-buffer count alone does not satisfy this criterion.
criteriaLedger.afterText: Match emitted TAP bytes, last-write clock/line, remainder, image position/size/dirty state, counters and failure/STOP effects for RECORD-before-motor and motor-before-RECORD, same/future-clock first edges, short gaps 0/6/7/8/2046/2047, long gaps at and above 24-bit boundaries, TAP v0/v1/v2 output paths, and first/partial/failed writes. Preserve the native first-gap and truncation behavior. Include the pinned stream-cursor versus logical-position command-order and buffer-boundary contract in FR-TAP-004 ac-04; retained buffered-read state is part of the initial condition.

criteriaLedger.beforeText: Use the FR-RUNTIME-TAPE-002 ac-01 media/control matrix to assert accepted mode, sense state, and unchanged state for ignored RECORD commands; do not treat an unconstrained RecordPressed flag as proof that RECORD was accepted.
criteriaLedger.afterText: Apply FR-RUNTIME-TAPE-002 ac-01 media/control matrix to accepted transport state and sense. Ignored RECORD is not a RecordPressed success. Include enabled-state gating and unchanged observations.

criteriaLedger.beforeText: Use FR-RUNTIME-TAPE-002 ac-02 observations to assert the C64 CPU-port and VIC-20 VIA1 input bits for both data-direction settings; separately assert pulse routing to C64 CIA1 FLAG and VIC-20 VIA2 CA1.
criteriaLedger.afterText: Apply FR-RUNTIME-TAPE-002 ac-02 and ac-07 to separate machine sense inputs, read-pulse interrupt inputs and motor/write outputs, including direction registers, raw VIC-20 PCR behavior and SX-64.

criteriaLedger.beforeText: Use the same recording eligibility traces as FR-RUNTIME-TAPE-002 ac-05. Assert emitted writes and absence of writes as well as updated last-write-line state, including input transitions while recording is ineligible.
criteriaLedger.afterText: Apply FR-RUNTIME-TAPE-002 ac-05 to ordered recording eligibility and write edges; assert output absence as well as writes and retained line state. Native running state is distinct from control input and completed startup delay.

criteriaLedger.beforeText: Use the same recording byte/error traces as FR-RUNTIME-TAPE-002 ac-06. Preserve the pinned native first-write handling and encoded gap behavior, including known native quirks, without patching VICE or replacing expected values with managed output.
criteriaLedger.afterText: Apply FR-RUNTIME-TAPE-002 ac-06 to exact recording bytes and side effects, including both RECORD/motor orderings, first-edge clock handling, 24-bit truncation and failed/partial writes.

criteriaLedger.beforeText: Assert the native startup schedule at t+32000 from a stopped motor with no pending alarm, and assert that a pending alarm is not overwritten by the start helper.
criteriaLedger.afterText: Assert stopped-motor ordinary startup at t+32000 with no pending alarm and preservation of an existing pending alarm. Observe callback dispatch separately from scheduled time; no first-Tick bypass. Exercise the separate command-entry path: START on an already-running motor invokes the start helper with and without media, schedules t+32000 only without a pending alarm, and preserves a pending alarm while still performing the native seek and write-state initialization. Distinguish command START from motor-line re-enable, and preserve the t+1000 alarm already installed by FORWARD/REWIND before their helper call.

criteriaLedger.beforeText: Assert motor-off at t on a running motor retains running state before the stop executes at t+32000, and that repeated motor-off preserves the first deadline.
criteriaLedger.afterText: Assert motor-off sets t+32000 stop deadline, retains a pending alarm and running state until a callback executes at or after that deadline, and repeated motor-off does not extend it. criteriaLedger.beforeText: Assert motor-on before pending stop execution clears the stop deadline and preserves running state without another startup delay; assert motor-on after an executed stop schedules a new native startup alarm.
criteriaLedger.afterText: Assert motor-on cancels a stop not yet executed, including after the nominal deadline but before a late callback, without imposing a new startup delay on an already-running motor. After an executed stop, obey the ordinary start helper and its pending-alarm preservation. Include cancellation before the deadline and same-clock cancellation before callback dispatch as separate cases from cancellation after the deadline; for an already-running motor, preserve the existing alarm and write state and clear only the stop deadline in this path.

criteriaLedger.beforeText: Compare ordered pulse and motor-state traces at deadline-1, deadline, and deadline+1 using fixed clock/control/alarm order. Do not use a first-Tick bypass or an unconditional off/on ramp reset as a substitute for native behavior.

criteriaLedger.beforeText: Named cases MotorOff_DelayedStop, MotorOff_RepeatedDoesNotExtend, MotorOn_CancelsPendingStop, and MotorOn_AfterExecutedStop_Restarts assert state and event order at deadline-1, deadline, and deadline+1. criteriaLedger.afterText: Run all named delayed-stop and cancellation cases in the amendment ledger, retaining deadline and callback boundaries separately. criteriaLedger.afterText: TransportSense_MediaCommandMatrix covers five commands from STOP, absent/read-only/writable images, enabled-state sense gating and later STOP. Reject wrong polarity, ignored-command state changes and missing transitions.

criteriaLedger.beforeText: Bit 3 of $0001 controls the motor: 0 = motor on, 1 = motor off.
criteriaLedger.afterText: C64 CPU-port bit 5 controls active-low motor output as !((DDR & DATA) & 0x20); input direction drives motor-on. Bit 3 is tape write, not motor. VIC-20 and SX-64 behavior follows FR-RUNTIME-TAPE-002 ac-07.

criteriaLedger.beforeText: The tape position advances only when the motor is running and spin-up is complete.
criteriaLedger.afterText: Tape motion, read-pulse delivery and stopping match the ordered native transport/alarm trace, including late stop execution and pending-alarm cases. criteriaLedger.afterText: PLAY/sense is not a prerequisite for asserting the native motor-running flag. Cover motor-on in STOP and RECORD, and distinguish transport mode/sense from motor control and running state.

criteriaLedger.afterText: Motor state changes are reflected in the `ITapeUnit.MotorState` property.

criteriaLedger.afterText: Tape audio remains required. criteriaLedger.beforeText: TAP v0 files are correctly parsed: each byte represents a pulse half-period in units of 8 system clock cycles.
criteriaLedger.afterText: For nonzero TAP bytes, preserve native pulse units and layer-specific conversion: file/block decoding uses pulse units while live datasette gaps use byte times eight before resource adjustments. Do not globally label every v0 byte a half-period.

criteriaLedger.afterText: Configured C64/VIC-20 file-decoder CBM pulse-unit ranges are inclusive 36-54 short, 55-73 middle and 74-100 long. Test endpoint and adjacent values after tap_init conversion. Keep live pulse clocks separate; do not pair inconsistent fixed cycle counts with TAP byte values.

criteriaLedger.beforeText: The standard Commodore tape header (FOUND marker), data blocks, and checksums are readable.
criteriaLedger.afterText: Pinned standard Commodore header, data-block and checksum workloads produce the same decoded bytes/status and machine-visible load outcome as native VICE. Include malformed, truncated and checksum-error fixtures.

criteriaLedger.afterText: Capture qualifying native write-line transitions from C64 CPU-port bit 3 and VIC-20 VIA2 PB3, including DDR-only changes, repeated/opposite edges and SX-64 disconnection.

criteriaLedger.beforeText: Written pulses are stored in TAP format with correct timing values.
criteriaLedger.afterText: Store the same bytes, gap/remainder, last-write state, file position/size/dirty state and counters as pinned VICE across short/long/24-bit boundaries and partial/failed output.

criteriaLedger.beforeText: The standard Commodore SAVE routine produces valid tape data.
criteriaLedger.afterText: A standard Commodore SAVE workload with pinned firmware, writable tape, resources and initial state produces the same bytes/status and machine-visible effects as immutable VICE, and its corresponding native/managed load results match. Include failure and write-protected cases.

criteriaLedger.beforeText: Writes can be appended to existing TAP files or written to new files.
criteriaLedger.afterText: New-image, existing-image current-position and explicit end-position recordings preserve the same prefix/suffix and file-position/size effects as native VICE. Existing-file writes must not silently become unconditional append or truncate. Retain RECORD accepted while the motor already runs as an in-scope sequence, including after buffered reads; that command does not itself seek. Distinguish the actual C stream cursor from logical image position and compare the bytes and both positions that pinned native execution produces. Include RECORD-before-motor, motor-before-RECORD, read-then-RECORD, intervening START/seek, beginning/interior/end positions and buffer-refill boundaries. Pin the exact native binary, platform/C runtime, file mode, initial bytes and I/O prelude, and retain repeated native observations. Do not invent a platform-independent result, insert a compensating native seek, silently exclude an ordering or treat an unstable/unobservable result as a passing gate.

criteriaLedger.beforeText: The record interlock (RECORD + PLAY buttons) must be engaged for writes.
criteriaLedger.afterText: Writable-image RECORD acceptance is the native interlock; absent/read-only-image RECORD is ignored. Do not require an additional independent PlayPressed boolean once native RECORD mode is accepted. Motor-running and qualifying-edge conditions still apply.

criteriaLedger.beforeText: Address $0000 is the Data Direction Register (DDR); bits set to 1 configure the corresponding $0001 bit as output.
criteriaLedger.afterText: Address $0000 is the Data Direction Register (DDR); bits set to 1 configure the corresponding $0001 bit as output.

criteriaLedger.beforeText: Address $0001 bits 0-2 (LORAM, HIRAM, CHAREN) control PLA banking and are reflected immediately in the address space configuration.
criteriaLedger.afterText: Address $0001 bits 0-2 (LORAM, HIRAM, CHAREN) control PLA banking and are reflected immediately in the address space configuration.

criteriaLedger.beforeText: Bit 3 controls the cassette motor (active low).
criteriaLedger.afterText: On C64, the cassette motor output is active low from DDR-masked bit 5, !(DDR & DATA & 0x20), and the cassette write output is bit 3, (~DDR | DATA) & 0x08. Match pinned VICE's changed-effective-output detection for data and DDR writes, including input/output transitions and repeated writes. Do not exchange the motor and write bits.

criteriaLedger.beforeText: Bit 4 reads the cassette switch sense (active low).
criteriaLedger.afterText: Bit 4 reads the cassette switch sense (active low).

criteriaLedger.beforeText: Bit 5 is unused on C64 but reads as expected based on DDR/pull-up behavior.
criteriaLedger.afterText: On the C64 board, reading $0001 with DDR bit 5 clear returns bit 5 clear; with DDR bit 5 set, its output readback follows pinned VICE's port data/DDR calculation. Bit 5 is the motor-control bit, not an unused pin. Exercise both data levels, both DDR directions, and direction changes; do not substitute SX-64 floating-pin behavior for C64 behavior.

criteriaLedger.beforeText: When a bit transitions from output to input, the capacitive discharge timing (approximately 350 microseconds to decay) is modeled.
criteriaLedger.afterText: Unused CPU-port pins reproduce the pinned VICE C64/SX-64 charge and decay behavior: bits 6 and 7 on both boards use a deadline of the current CPU clock plus 350000 cycles plus an inclusive random value from 0 through 70000; SX-64 bits 3, 4 and 5 use 1500000 plus an inclusive 0 through 300000. Writing a pin while configured as output, including a repeated identical data write, or changing it from output to input captures its data bit and sets its deadline. Other DDR transitions do not reset that deadline. Reads of $0001 clear active retained charge only when the deadline is strictly less than the current CPU clock, and substitute retained charge only for pins configured as input; reads of $0000 do not perform this discharge. Preserve native board selection, random-state consumption order, unsigned 64-bit clock arithmetic and reset behavior. Do not replace the executed behavior with a fixed 350-microsecond delay, an unused 8500 constant, or host-time expiration.

criteriaLedger.beforeText: The `IMemoryMappedDevice` interface exposes the port to the address decoder.
criteriaLedger.afterText: The `IMemoryMappedDevice` interface exposes the port to the address decoder.

criteriaLedger.beforeText: KERNAL: SX-64 variant KERNAL ROM with different default colors (blue screen instead of light blue).
criteriaLedger.afterText: KERNAL: SX-64 variant KERNAL ROM with different default colors (blue screen instead of light blue).

criteriaLedger.beforeText: No cassette port: tape-related I/O port bits behave differently (cassette sense always reads "no tape").
criteriaLedger.afterText: The SX-64 board has no connected cassette port. Match pinned VICE's board-specific PLA inputs and suppress forwarding of motor, write and sense-out changes to tapeport devices. CPU-visible reads of bits 3-5 must still follow the native data, DDR and retained floating-capacitor state; neither permanently-high nor permanently-low input values are a valid universal substitute.

criteriaLedger.beforeText: Built-in 1541 drive: device 8 is always present.
criteriaLedger.afterText: Built-in 1541 drive: device 8 is always present.

criteriaLedger.beforeText: The 6510 I/O port bit 4 (cassette sense) is permanently pulled high.
criteriaLedger.afterText: For SX-64 CPU reads of $0001, each input-configured bit 3, 4 and 5 is replaced by its retained native data_set_bit value after native falloff processing. Reset clears those retained values. Output writes and output-to-input transitions seed the corresponding retained data bit, falloff flag and deadline as pinned VICE does. A flagged retained value clears on a read only when its stored deadline is strictly less than maincpu_clk: a charged input therefore remains charged at the exact deadline and clears on the first later read. Output-configured bits retain normal port readback. Match each bit independently, native RNG-dependent deadline selection, repeated writes, direction transitions, reset and read side effects; do not impose an always-high or always-zero sense bit.

criteriaLedger.beforeText: All other hardware is identical to the C64 NMOS profile.
criteriaLedger.afterText: All other hardware is identical to the C64 NMOS profile.

criteriaLedger.beforeText: Selectable via `IMachineProfile.LoadProfile("sx64")`.
criteriaLedger.afterText: Selectable via `IMachineProfile.LoadProfile("sx64")`.

criteriaLedger.beforeText: Turbo loaders using shorter pulse widths than standard (down to approximately 160 cycles per pulse) function correctly.
criteriaLedger.afterText: Turbo loaders using shorter pulses than the standard Commodore format, including the existing approximately-160-cycle workload obligation, function correctly with the same pinned C64 firmware, tape fixture, resources and initial state as native VICE. Do not impose 160 cycles as a parser minimum or normalize pulse widths to hardware estimates; cover representable values below, at and above 160 with separately asserted block-decoder units and native live scheduling/interrupt traces.

criteriaLedger.beforeText: Common turbo formats (Novaload, Biturbo, Turbotape, Cyberload, Pavloda) load successfully.
criteriaLedger.afterText: Common turbo formats (Novaload, Biturbo, Turbotape, Cyberload, Pavloda) load successfully. For each named C64 format, retain identified fixture and firmware hashes, resources, initial state, load entry/operation sequence, expected loaded bytes and machine-visible completion/failure observations. Native and managed results must both satisfy successful loading and match; two equal failures do not satisfy this criterion. A missing fixture, oracle capability or completion observation leaves the corresponding format unsatisfied, not waived.

criteriaLedger.beforeText: Custom pulse encoding schemes are supported through accurate pulse-level emulation.
criteriaLedger.afterText: Custom pulse encoding schemes are supported through accurate pulse-level emulation. Pin custom-stream bytes and their format-specific expected loading/output behavior independently of the managed implementation; compare ordered native and managed tape/interrupt/timer observations without converting the input into a recognized standard loader or normalizing its pulse widths. Include malformed/truncated and boundary fixtures with explicit expected outcomes.

criteriaLedger.beforeText: The CIA FLAG input timing is accurate to 1 system clock cycle.
criteriaLedger.afterText: For C64 tape workloads, reproduce the exact native ordered CIA1 FLAG invocation, interrupt/timer state and clock observations at the approved observation boundary, with pinned main-CPU clock, alarm scheduled/dispatch clocks and callback offset. Do not interpret the former one-system-clock wording as permission for a one-cycle divergence. Include same-clock ordering and pending interrupt state, with missing, extra, duplicated and shifted events rejected. VIC-20 VIA2 CA1 parity remains separately mandatory under FR-RUNTIME-TAPE-002 and FR-TAP-003; CIA FLAG terminology does not substitute for it.

criteriaLedger.beforeText: Half-wave and full-wave detection methods both work correctly.
criteriaLedger.afterText: Half-wave and full-wave loader detection workloads both work correctly against pinned native VICE. Keep file/block TAP-v2 pairing (including each truncated half) distinct from live playback, which follows selected-machine tape behavior rather than applying a universal two-to-one conversion. Preserve fixture-specific ordered pulses, direction/phase, timer and load outcomes under separately pinned media version/system/video tags and machine resources.

criteriaLedger.beforeText: Multi-speed loaders (that change pulse rates mid-load) are supported.
criteriaLedger.afterText: Multi-speed loaders that change pulse rates mid-load are supported. Use a single pinned workload with an explicit sequence of rate transitions and assert the whole load result plus ordered native-equivalent pulse, timer and interrupt observations across every transition; disconnected constant-speed subtests do not prove the mid-load behavior. Run each required PAL/NTSC profile with pinned headers and preserve native scaling or lack of scaling.

limitation: Read-only source and data comparisons, not runtime or mutation proof. Guard protocol and capacitor case matrices remain proposed, not executable acceptance.
